text:
kevin: Hey team — we started getting a spike of 401 invalid_api_key from our web app this morning. Backend logs show 'invalid_api_key' for a bunch of requests but our backend test calls with the same key succeed. Any ideas?

kevin: Quick background: we store the API key in a cookie (api_key) in the browser and send requests directly from the SPA to our /proxy endpoint which forwards to Redwood. Server-side forwarding uses the cookie value.

talia: thanks for the repro notes. can you paste the failing request headers (the ones the proxy sends to Redwood)?

kevin: sure — here's a curl capture from the proxy when a user request fails:

```
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> Host: api.redwood.ai
> User-Agent: RedwoodProxy/1.2
> Cookie: api_key=ABCD1234...
> Accept: application/json
```

kevin: and when we manually forward with x-api-key header it works:

```
curl -v -H "x-api-key: ABCD1234..." https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
# 200 OK
```

talia: interesting — so the key present as Cookie isn't accepted by the Redwood endpoint. our API expects either Authorization: Bearer or x-api-key header; cookies are not a supported auth mechanism. are you relying on the proxy to translate Cookie -> header?

kevin: yes, proxy is supposed to extract the cookie and set x-api-key on the outbound request. sometimes it does, sometimes not — looks intermittent and only for requests that arrive via our CDN.

juan: pinging infra — edge proxies can strip cookies under certain conditions (size, SameSite, or if the route is configured to remove sensitive headers). also some CDNs drop Cookie headers on cross-origin requests unless explicitly whitelisted.

edge-proxy-bot: config-check: route /proxy -> upstream redwood: cookie_whitelist not set, header_transforms include: remove-set-cookie = true, strip_cookie_headers = true

talia: that config explains it. if strip_cookie_headers=true the proxy won't forward Cookie to upstream, so the proxy's translation step never sees the api_key and the outbound request has no auth.

kevin: ahhh. how did this start? we rolled a CDN policy change last night to reduce header size for caching and that flip turned strip_cookie_headers on.

juan: quick fixes: 1) add explicit header transform in the edge to forward Cookie for /proxy (cookie_whitelist: ["api_key"]) 2) change proxy to read cookie on edge and set x-api-key header before sending upstream (recommended) 3) stop putting raw API keys in browser cookies (security risk).

talia: for immediate customer mitigation you can: - flip strip_cookie_headers=false for the /proxy route OR - add a rewrite that sets x-api-key from cookie in the edge config. We'll prioritize a short-lived rollback while you implement the safer change.

kevin: repro steps we used to verify:
1) With CDN policy active (strip cookies) -> browser request -> 401 invalid_api_key (redwood logs: "auth: missing api key")
2) Disable strip_cookie_headers or send x-api-key header in client -> 200 OK
3) curl with cookie directly to https://api.redwood.ai (bypassing our proxy) -> 401 invalid_api_key (Redwood API doesn't accept Cookie auth)

kevin: so two root issues: Redwood doesn't accept cookies (ok) + our edge was stripping cookies so proxy couldn't translate (bad).

talia: correct. Recommendations: - Do not rely on client-side cookies for raw API keys. Use a short-lived session token issued by your backend, or have backend-only calls include the x-api-key. - If you must use cookie-to-header translation, make sure the edge forwards the cookie to the translator or does the translation itself. - Rotate any exposed key and treat current key as compromised if it was in a JS cookie visible to clients.

kevin: thanks — rolling the temporary rollback now (flip strip_cookie_headers=false for /proxy). I'll follow up after we push the safer token flow.

juan: let us know if Redwood logs show fewer 401s after the rollback. we can also help review edge config.

kevin: will do. attaching a short log snippet from Redwood showing the earlier failures:
```
[2025-06-08T09:12:03Z] request_id=.. path=/v1/generate auth=none result=401 error="invalid_api_key"
[2025-06-08T09:12:07Z] request_id=.. path=/v1/generate auth=x-api-key user=acct-123 result=200
```

talia: perfect, that's consistent. marking this as triaged — please update thread when rollback confirmed and when you've rotated keys. :thumbsup:
